subject.title: [Refactor] Consolidate synthetic log formats across MCP service pipelines

question: Should the core OpenClaw tools MCP entrypoint and the Codex plugin compatibility MCP adapter expose an identical fatal diagnostic format?
rationale: Source establishes shared transport constraints but not shared user-facing fatal text, while repository policy assigns Codex-specific behavior to the owning plugin.

options.title: Keep owner-specific diagnostics
options.body: Retain separate entrypoint prefixes while continuing to share protocol-safe stderr routing and generic error normalization.

options.title: Create shared diagnostic API
options.body: Define a stable fatal diagnostic envelope in an owner-boundary-safe SDK surface, then migrate both entrypoints with focused failure-output coverage.

recommendation.title: Keep owner-specific diagnostics
recommendation.body: Retain separate entrypoint prefixes while continuing to share protocol-safe stderr routing and generic error normalization.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily affects the Codex supervision compatibility adapter and its plugin-owned contract.
